title: A console route stamp rewrites a TRACKED inbox file in the plane; a later origin commit on that path blocks the wave-boundary fast-forward
summary: F30 architecture review M3 (+ m7). RouteConsole rewrites the item in place (lifecycle/route.go), and inbox root files are tracked. When the console later retires or edits that item on origin, the plane's wave-boundary merge --ff-only refuses and the loop plans against a stale local main (cmd_loop_wavesync.go 'local tracked changes block the fast-forward'). The protected-surface breaker and failure_count bumps always had this shape; F30's no-work hand-off makes it routine. Lanes are unaffected (they base on origin), but the plane's own tree — the inbox triage reads, policy, the binary-refresh HEAD — goes stale.
fix: Now: (a) wave-sync names the routed inbox files when they are what blocks the fast-forward; (b) document the console retirement procedure as a plane-side step at a wave boundary (verify, land via the curation PR, discard the plane copy). Durable (an ADR-0074 follow-up): keep route stamps out of tracked files — e.g. a gitignored sidecar the console partition and the claim floor read. m7: when routing a skip_shipped or close-class drop, put the landing probe's result (lifecycle WithLanded) into routed_reason so the console confirms in batches — never auto-retire (a landed sha proves the commit exists, not that it implements the item).
acceptance: A wave-boundary fast-forward blocked by routed inbox files names them (unit pin on the sync's WARN)
The console retirement procedure is in docs/operations (plane-side, at a boundary)
Route stamps no longer dirty tracked files (sidecar) — or an ADR records why not
